sights.w: Temple of Aizen Myōō, the deity of love and marriage, whose 1597 Hideyoshi-rebuilt tahōtō pagoda is an Important Cultural Property and the oldest wooden building in Osaka city; its Aizen Matsuri (30 Jun–2 Jul) opens Osaka's summer festival season.

sights.n: Abe Ōji Shrine (阿倍王子神社)
sights.w: The only surviving Kumano Kodō 'ōji' waypoint shrine inside Osaka city, counted fourth of the 99 Kumano ōji and traditionally founded under Emperor Nintoku.
Meiji-era shrine to the loyalist Kitabatake Akiie and his father Chikafusa, near the site where Akiie fell in 1338; a quiet stop on the Abeno–Sumiyoshi tram walk.

sights.n: Spa World (スパワールド, Shinsekai)
sights.w: Giant Shinsekai bathhouse with themed European and Asian bath floors (17 hot-spring styles from 12 countries) plus a rooftop pool — Osaka's classic day-long soak.
Seven stepped lanes (Shingon, Genshōji, Kuchinawa, Aizen, Kiyomizu, Tenjin, Ōsaka slopes) down the western edge of the Uemachi plateau through Osaka's temple town — the city's best old-Osaka walk.
